candidates.change_summary: Remove the statement that sets balances[msg.sender] to 0 after the external call, so the user retains their balance after withdrawal.
Replace `balances[msg.sender]=0` with `balances[msg.sender]=1`, causing the balance to be set to 1 instead of 0 after withdrawal.

Remove the require statement checking the result of the external call, which can cause the balance to be zeroed even if the call fails (reverting on the require but leaving state unchanged if sender uses try/catch, or changing state if revert occurs before zeroing — here deletion prevents revert, always zeroing the balance regardless of call success).
Delete the line that sets balances[msg.sender] to 0, so the balance is not cleared after withdrawal.
Replace the call value from balances[msg.sender] to 0, so no ether is sent but the balance is still zeroed.
Delete the require statement in the modifier, removing the reentrancy lock check.
Delete the second assignment that unlocks, leaving the lock permanently set after one call.
Replace the unlock assignment with setting lock to true again, keeping the lock permanently engaged after one call.
